claims.text: In samples/.../Design/OrderNotifications.cs at stage-1, OrderPlacedTightlyCoupled has no constructor parameters and creates its EmailNotifier field with new(); OrderNotifications takes an INotifier in its constructor.
OrderService at stage-1 takes IOrderRepository and INotifier, both interfaces declared in DonHang.Domain; OrderService.cs has no using lines and names neither EF Core nor DonHang.Infrastructure.
AuthController.cs at stage-1 has using DonHang.Infrastructure; and takes DonHangDbContext (concrete, DonHang.Infrastructure) and JwtTokenService (concrete, DonHang.Api) in its constructor.

OrdersController at stage-1 takes OrderService (concrete) and IOrderRepository (interface); its using lines include DonHang.Domain and not DonHang.Infrastructure; the DI container creates it with registered services (OrderService registered with AddScoped in Program.cs).

A class that creates its own concrete dependency cannot be given a fake; many constructor parameters suggest (by SRP) several jobs; reaching into another project's concrete details tightens coupling. All are worth a review comment even if the code works.

self_check.notes: Retargeted to stage-1; example_files set (DECISIONS.md §3). No constructor in the repo has many parameters, so outline item 2 is prose only. No dependency-graph tools (depth_notes).
